tools.name: search_tools
tools.description: Find tools among the 909 marketing data tools of Whizbrew (social profiles, posts and comments, app stores, ad libraries, trends, shops, developer and web data). Ask in plain words, e.g. "tiktok comments of a video". Returns each tool's name, one-line summary, price, group and stats (how often it wo

tools.name: describe_tools
tools.description: The full input schema, output type, price and one example call for 1 to 10 tool names from search_tools. Free.

tools.name: call_tool
tools.description: Runs one catalogue tool that reads data. A call is charged the tool's listed price only when it is a hit (it answered with data). A miss (answered, nothing there) and a failed call are not charged. The answer's meta says which: outcome, price_micros (what was charged) and balance_micros.

tools.name: get_balance
tools.description: The prepaid Whizbrew credit of this account.

tools.name: request_tool
tools.description: Call this ONLY when search_tools found no tool that fits what the user asked; never when a tool fits. It passes the request to the Whizbrew team, who read every one to see what they can add. Free; no promise and no answer comes back, so tell the user it was passed on and go on by other means. Never

tools.name: report_detour
tools.description: Call this AFTER you answered when no single tool gave what the user asked and you had to chain several tools, settle for a worse one, or guess (also when you used request_tool and then got there another way). Say what the user wanted, the tools you used instead in order, and why that was worse. The

tools.name: get_quote
tools.description: A free quote before you spend: which tools do a goal, the calls in order, the price per call and for the quantity you state, and the cash needed beyond the balance. Never spends. The answer ends with `next`: one step you can read to your human.

tools.name: start
tools.description: Says whether this account is still an agent's (not claimed: it stops after 7 days) or a person's, its balance, and the one next step. An agent without a key starts over HTTP: POST /v1/agent/start (no email). Free.

tools.name: add_money
tools.description: Makes a hosted card checkout link for your human to add credit; give them the link, never pay it yourself. With payment_id instead of amount_usd it says how that payment stands (poll every 5 seconds until paid). Making a link is free.

tools.name: claim
tools.description: Two small steps. 1: {email} of your human gives a short link; they open it, confirm the email, and the page shows an 8-letter code. 2: {code} they read to you makes the account theirs for good, with its key and balance. Free.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "request_tool" references sensitive artifacts (password). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "claim" appears informational but accepts parameters (code) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_tools, claim · Private data: request_tool, report_detour · Public sink: start, claim.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_tools, claim · Private data: request_tool, report_detour · Public sink: start, claim

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
